properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/21/2020
Violation Code: 78a85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - The operator failed to prevent gas flow in the annulus. In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.
Violation ID: 977636
Permit API: 131-20567
Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Mehoopany Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial/Aerial Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/02/2022
Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr (Stepped) pressure build-up tests, (SPBUT) being performed on (5) of the (6) wells on the Cappucci pad. The Cappucci 4H, N 2H, 102H, N 4H and HJMM WYO 1H wells. The 2H is not involved in todays Pressure Build Up Tests. This is the 2nd round of SPBUTs since remedial Perf. and Squeeze work performed on the Cappucci 4H, N 2H and the 102H was completed on 6/14/22. SPBUTs were initiated on 11/28/22 @ ~ 10:00 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - The (20x13) annulus was shut in on 11/28/22 @ ~ 09:50 - 96 hrs - The progressive shut in for the (13x9) annulus was missed on 11/29/22, resulting in a 96 hr shut in for the (20x13) annulus - The (13x9) annulus was shut in on 11/30/22 @ ~ 09:50 - 48 hrs - The (9x5) annulus was shut in on 12/1/22 @ ~ 11:00 - 24 hrs - All (6) wells annuli were shut in at time of sampling. - Upon arrival I met with Creston Consultants reps. Jason Rajan and Dakota Manning and CALLC rep. Patrick Gardner. Starting at approx. 11:00, ending annuli pressures were checked using a Digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for all the Cappucci Pad wells. - Cappucci 4H (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 200 ppm dropping to 0% CH4; No sample taken (13x9): 23 psi..; 82% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:32 (9x5): 132 psi.; 75% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:36 - Cappucci 102H (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0% CH4; 400 ppm dropping to 0%; No sample taken (13x9): 0 psi.; 59% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:05 (9x5): 47 psi.; 74% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:08 - Cappucci N 2H (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 120 ppm and dropping to 0% CH4; No sample taken (13x9): 2 psi.; 59% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:16 (9x5): 13 psi.; 62% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:22 - Cappucci N 4H (20x13): open top, No bubbling (13x9): 0.0 psi.; 860 ppm and dropping to 0% CH4; No sample taken (9x5): 0.0 psi.; 19% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:51 - HJMM WYO 1H (20x13): open top, No bubbling (13x9): 0.0 psi.; 20% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:42 (9x5): 0.0 psi.; 33,740 ppm CH4; Sample colected @ 11:46 - All (6) wells (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened and venting to production tank and the (20x13) and the 2H (20x9) were opened and venting to atmosphere via Sentry valves @ 12:15 - The Cappucci 2H well has been recently plugged back, above the Lower Marcellus. The Shallower formations of the Lockhaven and Braillier have been perforated in order to produce the shallower gas. - Creston Consultants were requested by Operator to obtain gas samples from outside tubing, the (5 1/2"x 2 7/8") annulus and from inside tubing. - Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for the Cappucci 2H well. - Cappucci 2H (20x9): No sample taken (9x5): No sample taken (5 1/2x2 7/8): 284 psi.; 81% CH4; Sample collected @ 12:00 (2 7/8 tubing): 138 psi.; 77% CH4; Sample collected @ 12:05 (This is a (2) string well)

Inspection Date: 7/24/2024
Comments: On 07/24/2024 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Southwestern's (SWN's) Vanorder-Patrick (12 Pad) Well Pad in Herrick Township, Bradford County. The weather was 70 degrees and cloudy. Rain fell on the pad within the last24 hours. I arrived at 1035 hours. The site remains stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed. There are two post-construction stormwater management structures onsite. They appear to be functioning properly. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 192.8-262 us/cm. There was no evidence of any spills or releases. There was one produced fluid tank held within secondary containment onsite. There were nine gas processing units (GPUs) held within secondary containment onsite. There were nine wells capable of producing. There were each properly tagged with the American Petroleum Institute (API) identification numbers. There were numerous temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment onsite. Violations remain outstanding at this site from a previous release. Violation ID: 8164678
Permit API: 125-22304
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/06/2023
Comments: On November 6 2023, the Department conducted an inspection of the Cole 1 OG Well in response to an OGI referral of the production tank leaking what appeared to be production fluid. At the time of inspection, the well appeared to drilled and equipped for production. The well tag was present on the well head. During the inspection, it appeared the production tank had previously been leaking at a valve near the bottom of the tank, but did not appear to be actively leaking. Distressed vegetation was observed in an approximate 3 foot radius around the tank. Directly below the valve, there appeared to be an excess amount of fluid along with a thick oil based matter. A background conductivity reading was taken and was 0.15 mS. Conductivity readings were taken in the soil in the area of the spill. The readings were elevated in comparison to the background reading with readings of 0.25mS, 0.45mS, 0.39mS, and 0.46mS. Elevated readings were detected in about a 3 foot radius around the production tank. Prior to leaving the location, the Department contacted KPI Representative Joel Greco to inform him of the release. Mr. Greco indicated that they had already replaced the faulty valve, and estimated the spill was roughly 15 barrels of production fluids and impacted the ground roughly 8 inches in depth. He stated remediation was scheduled to begin on 11/8/2023. I recommended that the Operator take immediate action to remediate the area in accordance with the Department's current spill policy. The Department requests clarification as to what caused the release, the quantity and type of fluid released (including the oil based matter) and how this was determined, as well as how long it is believed the release was occurring. Please include the clarification information within the NOV response.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the failure to properly control production fluid (and/or other fluids) resulting in a release to the ground, as well as failure to report a release.

Comments: On September 18 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 3491397, 3387914, 3514511, 3543627, and 3595504. The findings were as follows:According to the Order issued to the operator by the Department for this site, the Operator shall completely restore the well site within 9 months after plugging.The well site was not restored during today's inspection. The site was not exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. According to the landowner, the site has not been restored to pre-existing contours.The well was plugged on October 7, 2021 according the the plugging certificate submitted by the Operator for this well. As such, the Operator was to completely restore the well site no later than July 7, 2022. E and S Plan has not been received by the Department as previously requested in IRs 3262679, 3387914, 3514511, 3543627, and 3595504.No E and S Plan was found on site. Although there has been additional growth since the Department's last inspection in July of 2023, lack of adequate uniform vegetation is still observed due to multiple areas of exposed soil and rock. There are several bare spots throughout the former well site that are lacking adequate uniform vegetation. No E and S BMPs are installed on site.The ground appears to be seeded in most areas, but 70% uniform vegetation has not been achieved at this time. Vegetative growth may be hindered by the amount of rock and gravel on site. The Department recommends the Operator take necessary measures to ensure 70% uniform vegetative growth is achieved for restoration of the site.Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding.

Comments: On 3/23/2026, an inspection was conducted in response to reported sloughing (IR 4163547) at the Schwotzer Arthur well site in Blaine Township, Washington County. The sloughing was reportedly discovered by the operator on 3/20/2026, on the cutslope above the access road. Range Resources representative Denny Furmanek was present at the start of this inspection. An Individual Erosion and Sedimentation permit (ESP) was issued by the Department for this site on 1/26/2024 and expires on 1/25/2029.The following was observed during the inspection:The sloughing was observed on the cutslope above the access road, as reported by the operator on 3/20/2026 (photos 3-6). This area appears to be approximately 15 feet in width and does not appear to immediately threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth. No pipeline markers and/or gas well equipment were observed below the slough. Temporary stabilization is applied to the slough. Furmanek reported that no additional soil movement has occurred since the slough was discovered. Repairs are reportedly expected to begin once the ground dries adequately to allow for machine operation. The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 2 and 7). Post-Construction Stormwater Management Best Management Practices (PCSM BMP) appear to be constructed in the locations shown on the approved ESP plan drawings (photos 15-21). The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) inspection log, and ESP approval letter are on site (photos 2-5). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Seven gas wells are on site that appear to be equipped for production (photo 12). Well 6H is equipped with a well tag with no observable evidence of a fluid leak to the ground around it (photos 24 and 25). The well and operator's information are displayed and visible on this well tag, as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h).The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (photo 12). The GPU/Vertical Separator Units on site are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photos 13 and 14). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022.Based on observations from this inspection, violations are being issued against the slough on the cutslope above the access road.The following information is requested from the operator:- What is being done in the interim (temporary stabilization)- What is being done in the future (permanent stabilization)Please coordinate with DEP Technical Services for any potential modifications to the approved ESP that may be necessary for addressing the slough.

Comments: This inspection is being conducted as follow up to inspection 2975835 in which violations were issued for the well not being properly labeled. WQS Trainee Andrew Zadzilko is assisting. Conditions on site are rainy and approximately 47 degrees. There appears to be several erosion channels on the access road which are leading to low spots in the access road causing stormwater to pool at those locations. One (Photo 1-4) appears to be discharging sediment laden water into a roadside ditch. Another spot along the access road (Photo 7) is discharging into a culvert which is in turn discharging it into a well vegetated area. The Department recommends that the operator remediate the discharge (Photo 1-4) immediately and maintain the access road in a condition that will prevent future erosion and sedimentation issues. The operator was contacted by the Department in regard to this discharge. The Operator advised that due to weather issues no work had been conducted to address accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues on the access road network. There appears to be a bare spot adjacent to the well site (Photo 11) which is collecting stormwater and discharging it into a well vegetated area. The Department is requesting more information on how this bare spot was formed. The Department also recommends that the operator permanently stabilize this area to prevent storm water from creating accelerated erosion channels or possible impacting WOTC. The site appears constructed and equipped for production. The well is labeled. There are no leaks, dead or distressed vegetation observed. Based on this inspection the violation for the well label will be closed as corrected. Additional violations are being issued for the accelerated erosion to the access road and discharge of sediment laden water to WOTC. Additional violations may be issued based on responses from the operator.

Comments: On September 23, 2025, the DEP conducted an inspection at the Schwotzer Arthur well site. This inspection was conducted in response to a Post-Drilling Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) that was submitted by the operator on August 6, 2025 for well 6H (125-29133). A notarized Landowner Waiver of Well Site Restoration was submitted with the WSRR, as sound walls currently remain onsite. Total Depth was obtained on November 17, 2024 according to the Well Record, therefore site restoration is to be complete by August 17, 2025.An Erosion and Sediment (E and S) individual permit (ESP07632300100E) was issued by the DEP for this site on January 26, 2024 and expires on January 25, 2029.The following was observed:Accumulated fine sediment from the access road was observed in the rock-lined channel along Rural Valley Road (photo 3). This sedimentation has not reached the storm culvert where it empties (photo 4). No accelerated erosion rills were observed on the access road and well pad at the time of inspection (photos 2, 9, and 21). Exposed soil was observed in several areas onsite which appear to require additional temporary stabilization (photos 6 and 19). The soil crack that was present on the southwestern fill slope of the well pad appears to be repaired. Riprap has been added to this location to improve drainage (photo 12). No toe bulge was observed below at the time of inspection. Repair work has been conducted on the slough that occurred on the well pad cutslope, with no loose sediment observed in the vegetated channel below (photos 14-18). What appears to be surface cracking was observed at the top of well pad cut slope (photo 20). This appears to be due to recent excessive dryness onsite. No toe bulge was observed belowThe Act 9 sign is fully visible at the entrance of the access road, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (photo 22). The GPU units onsite are equipped with interconnected drip pans (photo 23). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the DEP for use on 6/21/2022. Well 6H is equipped with a well tag and appears to be in production (photo 24). No evidence of fluid leaks to the ground around it was observed. There are six additional well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, Well permits, Individual E and S permit approval letter, E and S permit drawings, and E and S inspection log are onsite (photo 25). Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/31/2022
Comments: On January 31, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a site inspection at Inflection Energy TLC Well Pad due to a reported spill. Inflection Energy Zac Subra left a message for DEP representative Brad Kline at 1150 explaining that a rented GPU dump had a washout due to a gush of sand causing a leak of production fluid to form. The leak overflowed the containment and impacted an area of snow and pad surface near the southwest corner of the pad. The area of impact was about 25 yards by 10 yards. Conductivity of free standing liquid in the secondary containment for the GPU was over range of the Oakton multimeter. The maximum conductivity range for the meter is 20,000 uS/cm. The well pad surface was screened with a soil conductivity meter and the conductivity ranged from 800 uS/cm to 2,800 uS/cm. The production fluid did not appear to flow off the well pad edge. The operator of the rented GPU noticed the leak on January 30, 2022 but did not notice any breech of containment and reported it to Inflection Energy. Inflection Energy Zac Subra arrived the next morning to follow up and noticed some staining in the snow around the containment for the GPU. Inflection Energy then began to vacuum out the secondary containment and, remove to contaminated ice snow near the GPU. Mr. Subra said the Penn E&R will be out to the well site to delineate the area of impact on February 1, 2022. This spill causes violations of the Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. The DEP recommends beginning the Act 2 process due to the unknown volume of the spill.

Violation ID: 957719
Permit API: 063-34032
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Cherryhill Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/02/2022
Comments: On 6/2/22 at 0900 hrs., I conducted an inspection of Turm Oil, Inc.'s Paul Strong 4 well (API 063-34032) in Cherryhill Twp., Indiana Co. Mr. Bill Davis with Turm Oil was also present during the inspection. The inspection was conducted in response to a complaint, received by the Department on 6/1/22, of oil and produced water being released from a production fluids tank that was being removed from the site.I spoke with the complainant, the operator, and Mr. Davis on 6/1/22. The operator informed me that the well was sold to Rosebud Mining back in March; however there is no record of a well transfer filed with the Department. During our phone call, Mr. Davis informed me that the tank removal and release occurred around 1100 hrs. on 5/31/22. He estimated that approximately 10 gallons of crude oil and production fluid was released when removing the tank, and stated that some absorbent material was placed near the well and was subsequently containerized. Mr. Davis also acknowledged that some released fluid was covered up during regrading of the site.Upon inspection of the site, oil stained soil and vegetation was observed, beginning at the regraded area of the well pad, and continuing along a drainage ditch adjacent to the pad. There was a strong crude oil odor present. The impacted water in the ditch flowed to a nearby ephemeral stream where a slight sheen was observed. The black plastic bag containing the absorbent material Mr. Davis previously applied was located at the base of the well head; however, no additional measures were taken to prevent the material from reaching Waters of the Commonwealth. I advised Mr. Davis to place absorbent boom or pads to prevent further downstream impacts. I also advised Mr. Davis that regulations require removal of the pollutant from the soil and water within 15 days. In addition, I requested that Mr. Davis reinstall a well tag with the permit number on the well head.The release was not reported to the Department. Violations of 91.33(A), 78.66(a), 91.34(A), 78.66(b), and78.66(e) are cited and will be immediately closed as 'unresolvable'.Violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), CSL 402(b), 78.54, 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(a), and SWMA 610(1) are being cited for the release of crude oil and production fluid onto the ground and into Waters of the Commonwealth. These violations will be resolved upon remediation and temporary stabilization of the site, and submission of waste manifests for the disposal of impacted material to the Department.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 07/29/2020
Comments: The Department was made aware on Tuesday, July 21, 2020 by an adjacent unconventional well operator of a communication incident impacting two offset unconventional wells operated by the adjacent operator. The adjacent operator reported two active producing wells, permit numbers 125-26943 and 125-26945, received a measurable transfer of fluid and pressure from the CNX Gas LLC, RHL28-GHSM (API 059-27830), an offset unconventional well currently undergoing hydraulic fracturing. According to the adjacent offset operator, observations of fluid and pressure were observed at the two wells beginning on or around on July 15, 2020. According to the adjacent offset operator, unconventional wells 125-26943 and 125-26945, are within the zone of influence of the RHL28-GHSM (API 059-27830) unconventional well currently undergoing hydraulic fracturing. The adjacent operator reported to the Department that CNX Gas LLC, was notified on July 20, 2020 of the communication incident by the adjacent operator. The Department previously received an electronic notification from CNX Gas LLC, that stimulation activities would begin on the RHL28-GHSM on Thursday, July 9, 2020 at 6:00 pm. The Department contacted CNX Gas LLC, on Tuesday July 21, 2020 regarding the communication incident. The Department informed CNX Gas LLC, of the notification and reporting requirements required by 78a.73(c). CNX Gas LLC, personnel indicated they are aware of the communication incident and are coordinating with the adjacent operator. To date, the Department has not received an electronic notification of the well communication incident in accordance with 78a.73(c).The Department reviewed the Area of Review (AOR) report deliverables as required by 78a.52a(c) and the as-drilled well plats and well records for the RHL28-GHSM (API 059-27830). According to the as drilled plats, 125-26943 and 125-26945 are within the AOR zone of influence of the RHL28-GHSM (API 059-27830). The AOR Summary Report information submitted to the Department on August 9, 2019 for the RHL28-GHSM (API 059-27830) failed to identify 125-26943 and 125-26945 as offset unconventional wells located within the zone of influence.After review of all available information, the Department issuing the following violations. See Notice of Violations section below.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Huntley & Huntley Inc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-01-03
Violation Code: 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
Violation ID: 879607
Permit API: 003-21968
Unconventional: No
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Frazer Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-03-02
Comments: This inspection is being conducted as a follow up to inspection 2995336 conducted on 2/10/2020 in which sediment laden storm water was observed leaving the operators access road and entering a stream. Only the portion of the access road where the discharge was occurring is being inspected. PADEP Eric Norman is assisting and Operator representative Isaac Haky is on site. The access road appears to have been regraded and CFS put down in several locations. While the regrading has abated the accelerated erosion rills observed in previous inspections, the Department recommends that the operator stabilize the access road to prevent a reoccurrence. The operator appears to have laid down stone on the portion of the access road which was previously pooling water and no pooled water or discharges are observed at this time. Based on this observation the CSL violations will be closed as corrected/abated effective 3/2/2020. The operator has placed CFS on either side of the road with soil berms that do not appear to be stabilized. The Department recommends that the berms be stabilized or removed. Based on their proximity to water conveyances the possibility exists that in a stormwater event they could be washed off into WOTC. The Department also recommends that the operator install CFS per the E&S Manual detail 4-1. Based on this inspection the CSL violations will be closed as corrected/abated. No new violations will be issued for this inspection. A follow up inspection for the other outstanding violations will be scheduled for a later date.
